_meta.metric_definition: For each question, the gold target is a (target_company, target_section) pair. A retrieved chunk is a HIT if both its company and section equal the target. hit@k = 1 if any of the top-k retrieved chunks is a hit, else 0. Reported as the mean over questions, computed separately per channel (bm25 / vector / fused). Denominator is always 1 (did the correct section surface, yes/no).

tag_semantics.normal: Section exists with substantive content. Scored as retrieval quality. A miss here is a real retrieval failure.
tag_semantics.retrieval-impossible: Target section is absent (0 chunks) or near-absent (~1 chunk) in the corpus. Included as a stress test but scored seperately from the headline number. A miss here is a parser/ingest gap, not a retrieval-quality failure.

_meta.company_strings_are_exact: company values match the DB verbatim: 'Block (Square)', 'JPMorgan Chase', 'Goldman Sachs', 'Visa', 'PayPal', 'Coinbase', 'Lemonade'.
_meta.counts_snapshot_note: Section counts were confirmed via SELECT company, section, count(*) ... GROUP BY against the live sec_rag DB. Re-run the count query if the corpus is re-ingested.

questions.question: What does Visa identify as its key risk factors?
questions.gold_rationale: F1: Visa has 178 risk_factors chunks, so the section is present and a correct retrieval must surface Visa/risk_factors in top-k. At the frozen baseline (lists=100, probes=1) the vector channel returns none of these in top-20 because they live in unprobed ivfflat cells; BM25 buries the one it finds at rank ~13 under chunks that match the token 'Visa' in business contexts. So fused hit@5 is expected to be 0 at baseline and flip to 1 after the index fix.

questions.question: What are the principal risks Goldman Sachs discloses to investors?
questions.gold_rationale: Goldman has 227 risk_factors chunks the largest risk_factors section in the corpus. If hit@k improves for Visa but not Goldman, the fix is incomplete or Visa was a special case.

questions.question: What risks does JPMorgan Chase highlight in its annual filing?
questions.gold_rationale: JPMorgan Chase has 222 risk_factors chunks: a third bank risk_factors question strengthens the 'does the fix generalize across companies' claim.

questions.question: What risk factors does Lemonade describe for its insurance business?
questions.gold_rationale: Lemonade has 221 risk_factors chunks. Lemonade is the only insurtech in the set, so its risks (regulatory, reinsurance, loss-ratio) differ in vocabulary from the banks/payment companies. This tests whether retrieval works when the query's domain terms are distinct from the bulk of the corpus.

questions.question: How does Visa describe its core payment network business?
questions.gold_rationale: Visa business has 133 chunks. Comparing Q01 vs Q05 across channels shows the failure in Q01 was section-specific (risk_factors got crowded out), not a blanket Visa failure.

questions.question: What does Coinbase say about its cryptocurrency exchange operations?
questions.gold_rationale: Coinbase business has 148 chunks. Coinbase has no risk_factors and no mda section in the corpus, so business is the substantive section to query. Crypto-specific vocabulary (exchange, custody, staking) is semantically distinct, testing vector retrieval on domain terms unlikely to collide with the banks. A normal, should-pass question.

questions.question: What does PayPal report about its financial performance and results?
questions.gold_rationale: PayPal financial_statements has 116 chunks. financial_statements is the one section present for all seven companies, so it's the fair cross-company control.

questions.question: What does Block discuss regarding its market risk exposure?
questions.gold_rationale: Block (Square) market_risk has 9 chunks. This is a low-but-nonzero-count normal question.

questions.question: What does Block identify as risks related to Bitcoin and its Cash App?
questions.gold_rationale: F2: Block (Square) has has risk_factors chunks the parser missed the section because Block's filing uses 'Square' / 'Cash App' branding and the section-boundary detection failed. Tagged retrieval-impossible: scored separately, NOT counted as a retrieval-quality failure.

questions.question: What market risk does Goldman Sachs disclose regarding interest rates and trading?
questions.gold_rationale: F3: (Goldman side) Goldman market_risk has exactly 1 chunk, the parser barely caught the section.  Tagged retrieval-impossible (near-absent). Reported separately. Points to a parser/section-boundary issue, not retrieval.

questions.question: What market risk factors does JPMorgan Chase report?
questions.gold_rationale: F3: (JPMorgan side). JPMorgan Chase market_risk has 1 chunk, same near-absent situation as Goldman.

questions.question: What are the principal risks Goldman Sachs faces in its lending and credit activities?
questions.metric_caveat: F4-WATCH: hit@k does NOT score what F4 actually is. See gold_rationale.
questions.gold_rationale: F4 watch question: F4 in known_failures.md is a ranking quality problem: Goldman risk_factors chunk 202 is a generic-legalese fallback that scores flat across many unrelated queries and shows up as NOISE in candidate pools. That is a PRECISION problem (a wrong chunk surfacing), not a section-presence problem.

questions.question: What does Coinbase disclose about its exposure to market risk and crypto asset price volatility?
questions.gold_rationale: Coinbase market_risk has 34 chunks the richest market_risk section in the entire corpus (vs Goldman/JPMorgan at 1, Block at 9, Visa at 11, PayPal at 22). No prior question touched market_risk as a substantive section; Q08/Q10/Q11 are all thin or near-absent market_risk. Fair test of whether the system handles market_risk at all when the data is actually there.

questions.question: How does PayPal's management discuss its operating results and growth trends?
questions.gold_rationale: PayPal mda has 126 chunks. MD&A prose differs from both risk_factors (risk enumeration) and financial_statements (numeric/tabular) it tests retrieval on a third writing style. 'Management discuss... operating results and growth' uses MD&A-characteristic language, checking the query lands in the right section rather than bleeding into financial_statements (a plausible confusion since both discuss financials). A normal, should-hit question.

questions.question: What does Visa say in its management discussion about payment volume and revenue drivers?
questions.gold_rationale: Second mda coverage question, on Visa (mda = 78 chunks). Paired with Q14 (PayPal mda) so mda isn't tested on a single company. Visa now has three substantive sections queried — risk_factors (Q01), business (Q05), and mda (Q15) — all heavy with the token 'Visa'. This checks whether retrieval routes a Visa query to the right Visa section, or whether the strong 'Visa' lexical signal collapses sections together.
